title: Journalist & Whistleblower Privacy Security Checklist
metaDescription: Essential security checklist for journalists and whistleblowers. Protect sources, secure communications, and maintain operational security.
intro: Protecting sources and maintaining secure communications is crucial for journalists and whistleblowers. This comprehensive checklist covers essential security practices to safeguard sensitive information, communications, and identities from surveillance and legal threats.

items.task: Enable full disk encryption on all devices
items.why: Protects all data on your device if it's lost, stolen, or seized by authorities.
items.howTo: Enable FileVault on Mac, BitLocker on Windows, or LUKS on Linux. Use strong, unique passwords for encryption keys. Test recovery process before relying on it.

items.task: Configure secure boot and firmware passwords
items.why: Prevents unauthorized access to your system at the hardware level and stops tampering.
items.howTo: Set BIOS/UEFI passwords, enable secure boot in system settings, and configure automatic locking when device is idle for more than 5 minutes.

items.task: Keep operating systems and software updated
items.why: Security patches fix vulnerabilities that could be exploited by adversaries to access your system.
items.howTo: Enable automatic security updates, regularly check for firmware updates, and maintain an inventory of all installed software with update schedules.

items.task: Install and maintain reputable antivirus software
items.why: Protects against malware, spyware, and targeted attacks that could compromise sources or stories.
items.howTo: Choose enterprise-grade antivirus with real-time scanning, enable automatic updates, and perform regular full system scans weekly.

items.why: Ensures you can recover important work and sources if devices are compromised or seized.
items.howTo: Use encrypted external drives stored separately, employ cloud backup with zero-knowledge encryption, and test restoration procedures monthly.

items.why: Prevents unauthorized physical access that could compromise all digital security measures.
items.howTo: Use privacy screens in public, never leave devices unattended, employ cable locks when possible, and consider using decoy devices for travel.

items.why: Protects conversations with sources from interception by third parties or service providers.
items.howTo: Install Signal, Wire, or Element for messaging. Verify safety numbers with contacts, enable disappearing messages, and disable message previews on lock screen.

items.why: Email is easily intercepted without encryption, exposing sources and sensitive information.
items.howTo: Use ProtonMail or Tutanota for encrypted email, set up PGP encryption for existing accounts, and create separate email addresses for sensitive sources.

items.why: Phone calls can be monitored, and regular carriers may comply with surveillance requests.
items.howTo: Use Signal for voice calls, consider using burner phones for highly sensitive contacts, and avoid discussing sensitive matters on regular phone lines.

items.why: Metadata reveals who you communicate with, when, and for how long, potentially exposing sources.
items.howTo: Use Tor browser for web-based communications, route communications through VPNs, and vary communication timing and patterns.

items.task: Create separate accounts for sensitive work
items.why: Compartmentalizes communications and reduces the risk of connecting sources to your main identity.
items.howTo: Set up separate email addresses, messaging accounts, and social media profiles. Use different devices or browsers, and never cross-contaminate accounts.

items.task: Use secure methods for file sharing
items.why: Protects documents and evidence from interception and maintains source anonymity.
items.howTo: Use SecureDrop, OnionShare, or encrypted file sharing services. Avoid email attachments for sensitive files, and verify file integrity with checksums.

items.why: Ensures source authenticity and protects against disinformation or entrapment attempts.
items.howTo: Develop multi-factor verification methods, use code words or phrases, verify through multiple channels, and document verification steps securely.

items.why: Physical meetings can expose sources if not properly planned and executed.
items.howTo: Choose neutral locations, arrive separately, avoid surveillance cameras, turn off phones or use Faraday bags, and establish emergency communication protocols.

items.why: Protects sensitive documents from unauthorized access and maintains source confidentiality.
items.howTo: Use encrypted storage, implement access controls, regularly purge unnecessary files, anonymize documents when possible, and maintain audit trails.

items.why: Reduces digital footprints that could compromise sources or reveal investigation details.
items.howTo: Clear browser history regularly, use private browsing modes, avoid logging into personal accounts on work devices, and Use a privacy-focused browser for sensitive research.

items.task: Secure devices and data when traveling
items.why: Border crossings and foreign travel present unique risks to device security and data.
items.howTo: Use clean travel devices, backup data before travel, understand legal rights at borders, and consider using cloud storage accessible only after arrival.

items.why: Legal compulsion can force disclosure of sources and compromise investigations.
items.howTo: Know your legal rights, maintain relationships with media lawyers, understand shield law protections, and develop protocols for legal threats.

items.why: Quick response to security incidents can protect sources and preserve important information.
items.howTo: Create incident response plans, establish emergency contacts, practice data destruction procedures, and maintain secure communication channels for emergencies.

items.why: Hides your internet traffic and location from ISPs, governments, and other surveillance actors.
items.howTo: Choose a no-logs VPN provider outside Five Eyes countries, use OpenVPN or WireGuard protocols, enable kill switches, and test for DNS leaks regularly.

items.task: Use Tor browser for sensitive research
items.why: Provides anonymity by routing traffic through multiple servers, making it difficult to trace back to you.
items.howTo: Download Tor browser from official sources, use only HTTPS sites, disable plugins and JavaScript when possible, and never download files through Tor.

items.why: Prevents DNS manipulation and reduces tracking by using privacy-focused DNS providers.
items.howTo: Use DNS providers like Quad9, Cloudflare DNS (1.1.1.1), or OpenDNS. Enable DNS over HTTPS (DoH) in browsers and configure router-level DNS protection.

items.why: Unsecured WiFi connections can expose your communications and allow network attacks.
items.howTo: Avoid public WiFi for sensitive work, use mobile hotspots when necessary, verify network names with staff, and always connect through VPN on untrusted networks.

items.why: Browsers are common attack vectors and can leak identifying information about your activities.
items.howTo: Install privacy extensions like uBlock Origin, disable third-party cookies, enable strict tracking protection, and regularly clear browsing data.

pro_tips: Create multiple personas with separate devices and accounts for different types of investigations to compartmentalize risks and protect source identities.
Regularly audit your digital footprint by searching for your name and associated information online to identify potential security vulnerabilities.
Establish a 'canary' system with trusted colleagues - a regular check-in schedule that alerts others if you've been detained or compromised.
Practice your security procedures regularly, including data destruction and emergency communication protocols, so they become second nature.
Build relationships with security experts, digital rights organizations, and legal professionals who can provide support when facing sophisticated threats.
